compare_blocks.body:
Boundary of use: the two scenes are editorial fiction about sampling, covering only the organisation of information, the choice of evidence and communication. Structural and safety criteria are set by the test process and engineering standards; whether a leak rate is acceptable and whether the product can ship follow the acceptance requirements written in advance and the judgement of the responsible person, not type.

### ENFP and ESTP: choosing among three lid versions

(Fictional scene) Three versions have been tooled. All three pass the same leak test — filled, inverted for ten minutes, no seepage — and that is the shared floor with no room to negotiate. The difference lies elsewhere: the first looks best but takes force to open one-handed; the second opens easily one-handed but looks ordinary; the third sits between the two. In this fictional review, both people can use the same test report to ask different questions. One question is which patterns suggest problems in use, such as opening a lid with one hand on public transport. (Fictional scene) Both can state the goal, the constraints and the acceptance method; the difference is which kind gets written into the constraints.

compare_blocks.body:
The first misread uses speed of rejection as a clue. Rejecting the first version may be because it kept seeping, or because it does not suit the target user's one-handed use; speed of rejection says nothing about preference, only about the time pressure and the information available.

The second takes working with your hands for S and telling stories for N. An ESTP will also polish the wording of a selling point repeatedly, and an ENFP will also take a sample apart to find the fault. Hand skills and verbal skills are both trained, and neither is a basis for typing.

The third takes not reading the full report for a lack of rigour. Whether a report gets read depends on duty, on information channels and on whether this report answers the question; the same person behaves differently across projects, with no correspondence to four letters.

The fourth takes E for organising and P for procrastinating. E describes the direction of attention and energy, and either type may have nothing to say after days of overtime; P describes keeping the outward stance open, and either type can settle a conclusion when the deadline is at the door.
